title: Rounding of the Amount Moved Out by the Account's Interest History
content:
How the amount moved out of an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is rounded follows the interest history of the account: the count of interest entries posted to it in the twelve calendar months ending on the instruction date.

Where 3 or more interest entries posted in that window, the amount moved is rounded half up to the whole dollar. Where 1 or 2 interest entries posted in that window, it is truncated to the whole hundred dollars. Where no interest entry posted in that window, it is rounded half up to the cent.

Take a hypothetical amount of 5678.4900 USD before rounding. Under the first rule it becomes 5678.00 USD, the cents standing below the half dollar. Under the second it becomes 5600.00 USD, truncation to the whole hundred dollars discarding everything below the hundred rather than rounding it; an amount of 5699.9900 USD would become 5600.00 USD in the same way. Under the third it becomes 5678.49 USD.

A count of exactly 3 interest entries falls under the first rule, a count of exactly 1 under the second, and a count of 0 under the third.
